statewide.description: The Governor is Vermont's chief executive, responsible for managing state government, signing or vetoing legislation, appointing judges and cabinet members, and representing Vermont in national affairs.

candidates.name: June Goodband
candidates.bio: Ran for Governor in 2024 as the Green Mountain Peace and Justice Party candidate.

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
candidates.bio: An Oxford-trained economist and Strafford native, running for office for the first time.
notablePositions: Proposes publicly funded universal primary care, with the state paying providers directly
Would fund it with income-tax surcharges on high earners — 2% on income over $250,000 and 8% over $500,000

candidates.name: Dean Roy
candidates.bio: 14-year-old Stowe student, running with the newly formed Freedom and Unity Party. Coverage: Newsweek, Fortune, CNN.
notablePositions: Helped form the Freedom and Unity Party in 2026
Believed to be among the youngest people ever on a Vermont general election ballot for Governor

candidates.name: Phil Scott
candidates.bio: Phil Scott has served as Vermont's Governor since January 2017, winning five consecutive two-year terms. A former contractor and racing driver, Scott is a Republican who has supported abortion rights and signed gun safety legislation while vetoing several Democratic tax and spending proposals.
notablePositions: Supports abortion rights
Has signed gun safety legislation
Has vetoed several Democratic tax and spending proposals
Led Vermont's COVID-19 vaccine rollout, one of the fastest in the nation
Focus on housing affordability and economic development

statewide.description: The Lieutenant Governor presides over the Vermont Senate (but only votes to break ties), serves on several state boards, and becomes Governor if the Governor is unable to serve.

candidates.name: Molly Gray
candidates.bio: Former Vermont Lieutenant Governor (2021–2023).

candidates.name: John S. Rodgers
candidates.bio: John Rodgers was elected Lieutenant Governor in 2024 running as a Republican, after years as a Democratic state senator. He previously served in the Vermont House and Senate representing the Northeast Kingdom and has long advocated for Second Amendment rights.
notablePositions: Supports Second Amendment rights
Switched from Democrat to Republican before the 2024 race
Focus on rural Vermont issues and the Northeast Kingdom
Advocates for workforce development and economic opportunity

statewide.description: The Attorney General is Vermont's chief law enforcement officer, representing the state in legal matters, enforcing consumer protection laws, and prosecuting public corruption.

candidates.name: Charity R. Clark
candidates.bio: Charity Clark was elected Vermont Attorney General in 2022, becoming the first woman to hold the office. She previously served as Chief Assistant Attorney General. She has been active in multi-state coalitions on opioids, environmental protection, and consumer fraud.
notablePositions: First woman to serve as Vermont Attorney General
Active in multi-state opioid and environmental enforcement actions
Focus on consumer protection and corporate accountability

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won the Republican primary for Attorney General and later withdrew; Edwin Howell Kemon is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

statewide.description: The Secretary of State oversees Vermont's elections, maintains official state records, regulates professional licenses, and registers businesses and nonprofits.

candidates.name: Sarah Copeland Hanzas
candidates.bio: Sarah Copeland Hanzas was first elected Secretary of State in 2022. She previously served in the Vermont House of Representatives for over a decade. She succeeded Jim Condos, who served as Secretary of State from 2011–2022.
notablePositions: Expanded access to absentee voting
Modernized business registration systems
Advocates for election security and voter access

candidates.name: H. Brooke Paige
candidates.bio: Longtime Vermont Republican candidate.

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won four Republican primaries in August (Treasurer, Secretary of State, Auditor, and Attorney General) and later withdrew from three of them. Secretary of State is the one he's still on the ballot for.

statewide.description: The State Treasurer manages Vermont's finances, investments, and public debt, and administers retirement funds for state employees and teachers.

candidates.name: Mike Pieciak
candidates.bio: Mike Pieciak was first elected State Treasurer in 2022. He previously served as Commissioner of the Vermont Department of Financial Regulation and oversaw Vermont's pandemic stimulus distribution before becoming Treasurer.
notablePositions: Focus on fiscal responsibility and pension fund management
Advocates for Vermont housing investment programs

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won the Republican primary for Treasurer and later withdrew; Lynn LaFleur is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

statewide.description: The Auditor of Accounts independently audits Vermont state agencies, ensuring taxpayer money is spent efficiently, legally, and as intended. The Auditor reports to the legislature and the public — not the Governor.

candidates.name: Tim Ashe
candidates.bio: Tim Ashe has served as Auditor Doug Hoffer's chief deputy since 2021. He was previously Vermont Senate President Pro Tem from 2013–2021, one of the most powerful positions in Vermont state government, and ran for Lieutenant Governor in 2020.
notablePositions: Chief Deputy Auditor of Accounts since 2021 (under Hoffer)
Former Vermont Senate President Pro Tem (2013–2021)
Led major Vermont policy initiatives on housing, climate, and tax reform
Ran for Lt. Governor in 2020 (lost Democratic primary)

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won the Republican primary for Auditor and later withdrew; Ivar Kronick is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

federal.description: Vermont has a single at-large congressional seat in the U.S. House of Representatives. One representative covers the entire state, serving on congressional committees, voting on federal legislation, and directing federal funding to Vermont.

candidates.name: Becca Balint
candidates.bio: Becca Balint was elected Vermont's at-large U.S. Representative in 2022, becoming the first woman and first openly gay person elected to Congress from Vermont. She previously served in the Vermont Senate and as Senate President Pro Tem. She serves on the House Judiciary Committee and House Education and Workforce Committee.
notablePositions: First woman and first openly LGBTQ+ person elected to Congress from Vermont
Former Vermont Senate President Pro Tem
Serves on House Judiciary Committee
Focus on housing, climate, and workers' rights

candidates.name: Gerald Malloy
candidates.bio: Army veteran; previously the 2022 Republican nominee for U.S. Senate against Peter Welch.

stateSenate.description: The Vermont State Senate has 30 members who serve 2-year terms. The Chittenden Southeast district elects 3 senators, who pass state legislation, approve the state budget, and confirm the Governor's key appointments.
stateSenate.voteForNote: This district elects three senators, so you can vote for up to three candidates — from any party, in any combination.

candidates.name: Thomas Chittenden
candidates.bio: Thomas Chittenden grew up in South Burlington and previously served on the South Burlington City Council. He was elected to the Vermont Senate representing Chittenden Southeast and is directly connected to his South Burlington constituents.
notablePositions: Former South Burlington City Councilor
Grew up in South Burlington
Serves on Senate committees

candidates.name: Kesha Ram Hinsdale
candidates.bio: Kesha Ram Hinsdale has been Senate Majority Leader since January 2025 — one of the chamber's top leadership posts — and has announced she is running for Senate President Pro Tempore in 2027, the Senate's top job, now that Phil Baruth is retiring. She served in the Vermont House from 2009 to 2016 and has been in the Senate since 2021. She is the first woman of color to serve in the Vermont Senate.
notablePositions: Senate Majority Leader since January 2025
Running for Senate President Pro Tempore (the Senate's top post) in 2027
First woman of color to serve in the Vermont Senate
Focus on climate, housing, and racial equity

candidates.name: Virginia "Ginny" Lyons
candidates.bio: Virginia Lyons is a Vermont State Senator representing the Chittenden Southeast district. She has served in the Senate for multiple terms.
notablePositions: Experienced Senate member
Chittenden Southeast representative

candidates.name: Bruce Roy
candidates.bio: Retired IBM engineer and Air Force veteran.

candidates.name: Javen Sears
candidates.bio: UVM student and South Burlington High School class of 2020 graduate.
notablePositions: Recent SBHS graduate (2020)
UVM student

stateSenate.notes: Rohan St Marthe won a Republican nomination as a write-in candidate in the August primary.
